# Texas Sharpshooter Fallacy

**Page type:** detail page (single-row obj-table layout: text left ~40%, two stacked canvases right ~60%)
**HTML title tag:** Texas Sharpshooter Fallacy — Pseudoscience in Data Analysis

**Subtitle:** Hypothesis generated by data then tested on same data guarantees a result

## Section: Target Drawn Around the Bullet Holes After Shooting

- **Cancer clusters:** "There are 5 cancer cases on this street — it must be the power lines!" With millions of streets, some will have clusters by pure chance; the target was drawn around this one after the fact, not predicted in advance.
- **Feature selection:** "We discovered that Feature X perfectly predicts churn!" — after testing 500 features, where p<0.05 predicts ~25 false positives. One of them got a circle drawn around it and was called a discovery; the target was painted after the shot.
- **Epidemiology:** "Disease X is 3× more common in people who eat Y!" — one significant hit among 200 food–disease combinations, published as a breakthrough. The 199 non-results are invisible, so the published one is noise dressed as signal.
- **Algorithmic trading:** "Our backtest found a pattern: sell on the 3rd Tuesday after an earnings miss when VIX > 20" — after testing 10,000 pattern combinations. Some will fit historical data by chance; the coincidence was declared a strategy.

**Why it's pseudoscience:** A hypothesis generated by the data and then tested on the same data guarantees a result — you're confirming that the data contains itself. Real science derives the hypothesis from theory and tests it on new data.

### Visualization (canvas `c1`, 720×340)

Scatter of random bullet holes with a target drawn around one chance cluster.

- **Title (bold 17px, top center, `#1a5276`):** "Shoot First, Draw Target Later — Guaranteed Bullseye".
- **Bullet holes:** 30 small dark dots (`#333`, radius 3) at pseudo-random positions in the region x ∈ [100, 620], y ∈ [50, 180] (deterministic LCG random, seed 77).
- **Target:** three concentric red circles (`#e74c3c`, line width 3) centered at (380, 100) with radii 55, 35, and 15, drawn around one apparent cluster of dots.
- **Annotation (bold red 17px, centered at y=210):** "\"Look! A cluster! Clearly significant!\"".
- **Caption (gray `#555` 17px, centered at y=230):** "(Target drawn AFTER seeing where bullets landed. 500 features tested → 25 false positives expected.)".

### Visualization (canvas `c2`, 720×300)

Two-panel flow diagram contrasting the valid scientific method with the Texas sharpshooter loop.

- **Title (bold 17px, top center, `#1a5276`):** "Hypothesis Generation vs Confirmation".
- **Left panel ("Valid Scientific Method"):** green-outlined box (`#27ae60`, width 2) at x=20, y=30, 320×120; bold green 16px panel title centered at top. Inside, four step boxes 60×28 with 15px gaps, fill `rgba(39,174,96,0.15)`, green 1px border, dark text `#2c3e50` 16px: "Theory" → "Hypothesis" → "NEW Data" → "Test", connected by green arrows with filled triangular arrowheads. Bottom label in green 16px: "(independent data)".
- **Right panel ("Texas Sharpshooter"):** red-outlined box (`#e74c3c`, width 2), same size, right-aligned 20px from the right edge; bold red 16px panel title. Inside, five step boxes 50×28 with 8px gaps: "Data" → "Find pattern" (two lines) → "\"Hypothesis\"" → "SAME Data" (two lines) → "\"Confirmed!\"". Boxes 1 and 4 ("Data" and "SAME Data") use darker fill `rgba(231,76,60,0.2)`; the others `rgba(231,76,60,0.1)`; all have red 1px borders and `#2c3e50` 16px text; red arrows with arrowheads between steps.
- **Loop annotation:** dashed red quadratic curve (dash 3/2, width 1.5) arcing from below the "SAME Data" box back to below the "Data" box, with bold red 17px label "(same data twice!)" at the arc midpoint.
- **Bottom label (bold 18px, dark red `#c0392b`, centered at bottom):** "Using the same data to find AND confirm = proving data contains itself.".

## Regeneration instructions

- **Layout:** standard detail-page `.obj-table`: full-width table, one `<tr>`; left `<td>` (40%) holds `.obj-title`, bullets, and the "Why it's pseudoscience" paragraph; right `<td>` (60%, centered) holds two stacked canvases (`c1` 720×340, `c2` 720×300).
- **Page style:** body system sans-serif (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI'), white background, text `#2a2a2a`, padding 20px 10px, line-height 1.6; h1 1.6em `#1a5276`; `.subtitle` `#666` 1.0em; paragraphs `#333` 0.95em; `ul` 0.9em `#333` with 6px item spacing; table cell borders `1px solid #e0e0e0`, padding 20px 24px, vertical-align middle; `.obj-title` 1.05em, weight 600, `#1a5276`; `strong` in `#1a5276`. No nav bar, no back/home links.
- **Canvas:** declare intrinsic `width`/`height` attributes per chart; scale by `window.devicePixelRatio` (cap display at the logical width via `style.maxWidth`, backing store = rendered width × dpr, `ctx.scale` back to logical coordinates) via a shared `setup(id)` helper; `canvas { display: block; margin: 0 auto; }`. Chart draw functions are registered in a `__charts` array and re-run on window resize (debounced 150ms).
- **Palette:** primary blue `#1a5276`, green `#27ae60`, red `#e74c3c`, orange `#e67e22`, gray text `#555`/`#333`, dark slate `#2c3e50`.
- In regenerated HTML, any card links use `.html` extensions.
